title: Income Annuities Deposits Paid After a Death: Recovery and Direct Settlement by the Payee
content:
**From whom a post-death deposit is recovered.** On Ashgrove Income Annuities, a deposit paid to the surviving payee after the survivor continuation took effect is not asked back from the bank, because the payee entitled to the continuing payments received it; what is owed back on it is recovered from that payee. Any other deposit made after a death is first asked back from the bank within the tier's reclamation window, the rest being requested from the estate or the person who received it.

**Direct settlement.** The payee may settle the overpayment on such a deposit directly: the overpayment owed and the payee's repayment are recorded together against that deposit, and any part of the overpayment not repaid stays owed on the contract to be recovered by offset.

**Recording.** An overpayment on a deposit paid after a death is recorded once against that deposit. On a joint-and-survivor tier, the overpayment on a deposit paid after the first death is the part of it the surviving payee was not entitled to.

| Deposit | First recourse | Remainder |
|---|---|---|
| Paid to the surviving payee after the survivor continuation took effect | Not asked back from the bank; recovered from that payee | Stays owed on the contract, recovered by offset, where the payee does not repay it |
| Any other deposit made after a death | Asked back from the bank within the reclamation window | Requested from the estate or the person who received it |

**What the records show after a settlement.** The contract's activity history carries an overpayment entry for the amount owed on the deposit and a repayment entry for the payee's own repayment, both linked to that deposit; the overpayment owed on the contract rises by the overpayment and falls by the repayment.

## The payee's settlement tool: `settle_post_death_deposit_f655a739`

**Capability.** The payee who received an Ashgrove income annuity deposit that was too large after an annuitant's death settles, in person, what is owed back on it. One call records on the contract's activity history the overpayment owed on that deposit and the payee's own repayment toward it, both linked to the deposit; any part of the overpayment not repaid stays owed on the contract.

**How it is invoked.** This is the customer's own tool: unlock it with `unlock_user_discoverable_tool` and hand it over; the customer themselves — the payee — runs it with `call_user_discoverable_tool`.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `income_contract_id` | Reference number of the income annuity contract the deposit was paid from, from the income annuity contract lookup | Identifier as recorded |
| `source_txn_id` | Reference number of the deposit concerned, as shown on its entry in the contract's activity history | Identifier as recorded |
| `payment_due_date` | Scheduled payment date of that deposit, as shown on its activity entry | YYYY-MM-DD |
| `overpaid_amount` | The overpayment owed back on the deposit | USD, 2 decimal places |
| `repayment_amount` | The amount the payee repays now | USD, 2 decimal places |

**Return.** A receipt line beginning "Repayment recorded", with the contract and the deposit concerned, the reference numbers of the overpayment entry and of the repayment entry, the overpayment owed and the amount repaid in USD with 2 decimal places. That receipt means both entries are booked.
